extraction.description: SeamlessAlign is a multimodal corpus of automatically aligned speech translations. It contains more than 470,000 hours of data used to develop multilingual speech and text translation systems.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involved parallel data mining, where raw audio was chunked into segments, processed with language identification, and aligned with text data from the NLLB dataset by projecting both into a common embedding space to identify translation pairs.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of 4 million hours of audio from a public repository of crawled web data (approximately 1 million hours in English) and a sentence-segmented text dataset from NLLB.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The models exhibit gender bias, specifically overgeneralizing to masculine forms when translating from neutral terms and showing a lack of robustness when varying gender.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Limitations stem from the string-matching techniques used for toxicity and gender imbalance detection. Word list-based detectors can over-detect terms out of context, rely on precise tokenization, and lead to false negatives when combined with ASR. Furthermore, using linguistic gender clues as a proxy for overall gender representation is limited due to varying gender assignment rules across languages.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The work aims to promote accessibility and help individuals communicate and learn in languages where they have low proficiency by advancing massively multilingual and multimodal machine translation.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The evaluations and datasets involve sensitive human attributes such as gender, demographics, and speaker voice qualities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The datasets and models are used for training, fine-tuning, and evaluating supervised tasks (T2TT, ASR, S2TT, S2ST) and zero-shot tasks (T2ST).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The datasets were split randomly into an 80/20 train/test proportion, ensuring the same source audio or text remained in the same partition. Additionally, pseudo-labeling was used to generate synthetic speech from text to augment the training data and overcome data scarcity.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text data underwent cleaning and filtering. Audio data was deduplicated, resampled to 16KHz, and filtered to remove non-speech data using an audio event detection model. Audio files were segmented using a Voice Activity Detection (VAD) model, and any audio longer than 30 seconds was filtered out.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Starting with a large collection of raw audio, we chunked files into overlapping segments and applied speech Language Identification (LID). On the text side, we used the same sentence-segmented dataset drawn from NLLB [NLLB Team et al., 2022]. Speech and text corpora were then projected into a common embedding space, in which mining was performed to identify translation pairs with optimal segmentation.
